How does this differ from https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/45125

1. My change tries to find new privilege combinations in Subordinate map (first cycle at diff in parse_registries.py). Others don't.

2. Different variables naming for aliases in privilege_registry.hpp for new subordinate privileges. I'm not sure who named it better. I tried to describe all subordinate subsequence.

3. My change has no usage of new privileges. Maybe I will push its usage later as another change.

Ok.... I've got some awkward questions here.  Does anyone actually care about the privilege registry for non-admin users?  The only use cases I see most of the time are Admin and Read-Only.  Nobody has tried to sort out the whole problem where Operator Privilege has a lot more permissions than it should.

I really do appreciate the work, but it would be good to know where you're wanting to go with this.

I think - the key question may be - is https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/45125 incorrect?
If not, I think it would be better to add the review and suggestion to 45125,

For a given example, https://redfish.dmtf.org/registries/Redfish_1.5.0_PrivilegeRegistry.json 
```
      {
            "Entity": "LogEntry",
             "SubordinateOverrides": [
               {
                    "Targets": [
                        "Chassis",
                        "LogServiceCollection",
                        "LogService",
                        "LogEntryCollection"
                    ],
                    "OperationMap": {
                       "PATCH": [
                            {
                                "Privilege": [
                                    "ConfigureComponents"
                                ]
```

- This commit produces

```
const static auto& patchLogEntrySubLogEntryCollectionSubLogServiceSubLogServiceCollectionSubChassis = privilegeSetConfigureComponents;
```

- commit 45125 produces

```
const static auto& patchLogEntrySubOverChassisLogServiceCollectionLogServiceLogEntryCollection = privilegeSetConfigureComponents;
```

Basically, the key difference is on the naming - which is reversed each other, and where to put they keyword "Sub" (or "Subover").

I think it is more natural to name it as in "Targets" and put "Sub" before "Targets" as in the DMTF spec.

I don't think the spec implies each element in Targets is subordinated each other, but the "Entry" is subordinated in the path of "Targets".

So

```
LogEntry: Subordinates over [ Chassis - LogServiceCollection - LogService -]
LogEntryCollection```
rather than 
```
patchLogEntry Subover LogEntryCollection Subover LogService Subover LogServiceCollection Subover Chassis
```

Exactly. Operator has lot more permissions. 
I was solving a problem where the operator could change network settings. Operator should not be able to do this because of subordinate privileges according to dmtf privilege registry.
And yes, I saw some discussions about operator role. Someone from dmtf wrote that they were thinking about eliminating this role at all. 
But this doesn't solve a problem, when bmcweb ignores subordinate overrides for privileges.
So I created a change to parse subordinate overrides, but not to use it for now.

Seems like 45125 is incorrect. Because it will break as soon as unique combinations of privileges are created in subordinate overrides.


I didn't see 45125 when I pushed my changes, so I don't know what would be better - to give the suggestion to 45125 or merge this change, because it already contains this fix. Maybe you can quickly merge my change and then and the Author of 45125 will just use them for his purposes 😄.


As for naming. Subordinate overrides applies to redfish urls if the path contains all of targets.
So, the given example for LogEntry will be applied to "/redfish/v1/../Chassis/LogServiceCollection/LogService/LogEntryCollection/LogEntry". It may contain additional keys in the path if I understand dmtf spec correctly. I applied reverse order, because the last part of whole path is Entry, and it is at the beginning of the variable name. 
But as I said earlier, I'm not sure which naming is better. And I will not strongly defend my position on this issue. If you want to accept my work, I can rename the variables.
>Seems like 45125 is incorrect. Because it will break as soon as unique combinations of privileges are created in subordinate overrides.

>Seems like 45125 is incorrect. Because it will break as soon as unique combinations of privileges are created in subordinate overrides.

I'm sure about this. Where is it breaking? -- it would be better to add such comment to 45125.

BTW, the outputs are the same (although the variable names may be different).


>I didn't see 45125 when I pushed my changes, so I don't know what would be better - to give the suggestion to 45125 or merge this change, because it already contains this fix. Maybe you can quickly merge my change and then and the Author of 45125 will just use them for his purposes 

45125 is currently under review. Please add your comment to it and suggest what's wrong with it.

>As for naming. Subordinate overrides applies to redfish urls if the path contains all of targets.

As shown as an example of DMTF spec, the naming scheme is like
```
 <operation><Entity> SubOver <Targets>
```

For example, it will be like
```
patch LogEntry SubOver ChassisLogServiceCollectionLogServiceLogEntryCollection
```
where operation = patch, Entity= LogEntry, Targets =

```
       "Targets": [
                        "Chassis",
                        "LogServiceCollection",
                        "LogService",
                        "LogEntryCollection"
                    ],

```

I think it is more natural to the spec, and easier to read (than reversing the target list).

IBM doesn't care about Operator today, although we would support it if the permissions got figured out. Only Admin and ReadOnly today for us. I still think this support (SubordinatePrivileges) is useful.
Typically we go with the change that was up for review first unless there is a reason not to. Can you review 45125 ?
My employer cares to this. Someone is using operator role.
Sounds reasonable. Ok, I'l push a suggestion to 45125.

> BTW, the outputs are the same (although the variable names may be different).

Yes, because right now Subordinate Override sections do not have unique privileges combinations.

Yep.  This was the soft plan, because it wasn't clear anyone was using it correctly to its intended effect.

If there are duplicates in DMTF spec, I think it should be addressed in DMTF first.
If not, this code is basically choosing an arbitrary one without noticing it. 

I think it is better based on what is in DMTF.  This also helps to make sure to have the correct DMTF spec If there are invalid cases in spec.

As I said to another thread:

> No, there are no duplicates.. I'll try to explain what I ment.
> 
> 
> scripts/parse_registries.py has 2 cycles over privilege registry. 
> The first one finds unique combinations of privileges at DMTF's spec and creates privilege_dict. Then this will turn into code in redfish-core/include/registries/privilege_registry.hpp:22-50.
> The second cycle created aliases to this dict entries and turn it to the code at the rest of redfish-core/include/registries/privilege_registry.hpp.
> 
> 
> So my change has an insertion to both cycles. First change appends to privilege_dict unique combinations, second change creates alises for subover targets.

Right now the first cycle at my change of scripts/parse_registries.py does nothing, because all privilege combinations at SubordinatteOverrides already in privilege_dict, because they were found earlier without taking into account SubordinatteOverrides. But the next version of DMTF's spec may contain new combinations in SubordinatteOverrides.

FWIW, the intention of DMTF and of me personally is to just disable this stuff.  I understand that companies are large and you're just following orders, but if there's anyone that could speak to your guys intentions with this stuff, it would likely help you avoid a lot of rework in the future.

I think the key point is:

>Right now the first cycle at my change of scripts/parse_registries.py does nothing, because all privilege combinations at SubordinatteOverrides already in privilege_dict, because they were found earlier without taking into account SubordinatteOverrides

In other words, a new operation (e.g. "NewPrivilege") is used as a part "SubordinateOverrides" of an entity, not in the other entities?
Is it possible (or valid) in DMTF spec?
If so, the part can be added to 45125.

45125 has a long history of the discussion and endeavor and it is appropriate to keep those, and accumulate more to it as added.

> In other words, a new operation (e.g. "NewPrivilege") is used as a part "SubordinateOverrides" of an entity, not in the other entities?

Thanks. I've incorporate this part into https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/45125

I asked my colleagues. They use  operator role when it is necessary to have user with an access to controls and some settings, such as kvm or event logs or creating a read-only user, but he shouldn't have access to settings, which could break access to BMC (network, firmware updating ...).


For example: Admins have root role and could do anything. But on the client side there is not only an ordinary user to monitor the server, but also its own administrator, who should have more rights, but should not be given full access.


However, I personally agree with your opinion that the operator role is questionable and can be removed.

> They use operator role when it is necessary to have user with an access to controls and some settings, such as kvm or event logs

kvm functionally gives full privileges to the BMC, as the user can simply create an administrator account.  The existing privilege registry also gives operator level users access to some settings, and the distinction isn't clear.

> I personally agree with your opinion that the operator role is questionable and can be removed.

No, there are no duplicates.. I'll try to explain what I ment.


scripts/parse_registries.py has 2 cycles over privilege registry. 
The first one finds unique combinations of privileges at DMTF's spec and creates privilege_dict. Then this will turn into code in redfish-core/include/registries/privilege_registry.hpp:22-50.
The second cycle created aliases to this dict entries and turn it to the code at the rest of redfish-core/include/registries/privilege_registry.hpp.


So my change has an insertion to both cycles. First change appends to privilege_dict unique combinations, second change creates alises for subover targets.
